road.title: Shopping
road.place: The Quiet Hollow beyond the Hedge
road.description: A thin, anxious presence wearing a waistcoat the colour of old tea, beside a folding table and a sign that is nearly spelled right. Cuthbert is a Shopkeeper of the Last One and has exactly one of everything left and is in no hurry to part with it.

road.description: A thin, anxious presence wearing a waistcoat the colour of old tea, beside a folding table and a sign that is nearly spelled right. Cuthbert is a Shopkeeper of the Last One and has exactly one of everything left and is in no hurry to part with it.

openObjectives.prompt: Cuthbert has been standing at your elbow since you came in, radiating helpfulness. Tell Cuthbert what you are looking for: a shirt, a jacket, a hat, a pair of shoes, using Italian.
Ask Cuthbert whether you can try it on, using Italian.
Cuthbert is holding up two of them and plainly prefers the dearer. Tell Cuthbert which one you want: this one or that one, using Italian.

character.name: Cuthbert Marrow
character.description: A thin, anxious presence wearing a waistcoat the colour of old tea, beside a folding table and a sign that is nearly spelled right. Cuthbert is a Shopkeeper of the Last One and has exactly one of everything left and is in no hurry to part with it.

npc.narrative: It is notte, and the stelle hang over the siepe like merce not yet priced. In the bottega, one lampada, one sgabello and one banco wait for you. Cuthbert Marrow looks up from a grande libro and reads the ultima riga back to the stanza.
npc.native: Buonasera, sono Cuthbert Marrow, e questo è il mio negozio. Ho una camicia, una giacca, un cappello e un paio di scarpe, ma solo uno di ogni cosa. Io non posso provare le scarpe per te, e quello è il mio libro, non toccare. Che cosa cerchi stasera, e com'è la strada di notte?
npc.translation: Good evening, I am Cuthbert Marrow, and this is my shop. I have a shirt, a jacket, a hat and a pair of shoes, but only one of each thing. I cannot try the shoes on for you, and that is my book, do not touch it. What are you looking for tonight, and what is the road like at night?

player: Buonasera! La strada è buia e fredda. Cerco una giacca, per favore.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You greeted Cuthbert, described the cold dark street and told him you are looking for a jacket, all in good Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: "Cerco una giacca" tells Cuthbert what you are looking for.
You haven't asked yet whether you can try it on; Cuthbert will ask for this again later.
You haven't said which one you want, this one or that one; Cuthbert will ask for this again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Cuthbert whether you can try it on, using Italian.
Cuthbert is holding up two of them and plainly prefers the dearer. Tell Cuthbert which one you want: this one or that one, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Cuthbert opens the libro with the care of a man defusing a pie, and writes your words down. Behind him the giacca hangs on its hook, the only one, looking watched. Outside the stelle are out, and the strada runs a little straighter toward the porta.
npc.native: Scrivo nel libro: «La strada è buia e fredda». Giusto. Questa è la giacca, l'ultima che ho, e quella è la camicia, anche l'ultima. Io posso provare la giacca ogni sera, ma per te è diverso: che cosa pensi della giacca, e come ti sembra il mio negozio?
npc.translation: I write in the book: "The road is dark and cold." Correct. This is the jacket, the last one I have, and that is the shirt, also the last one. I can try on the jacket every evening, but for you it is different: what do you think of the jacket, and how does my shop seem to you?

player: La giacca è bella. Posso provarla?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely work: you gave your opinion of the jacket and asked to try it on, all in good Italian. Next, try pointing out which item you want.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you asked Cuthbert if you can try it on, and "Posso provarla?" is correct.
You haven't yet told Cuthbert which one you want, this one or that one. He will ask you again later, so have a go then.

openObjectives.prompt: Cuthbert is holding up two of them and plainly prefers the dearer. Tell Cuthbert which one you want: this one or that one, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Under the stelle, Cuthbert lifts the giacca off its hook and holds it at arm's length, like a man lending a kidney. The libro lies open on the banco, its last riga still faintly damp. He reads it back to himself, twice, in case you have changed.
npc.native: Scrivo nel libro: «La giacca è bella. Posso provarla?» Sì, puoi provare la giacca, ma solo una volta. Questo è il mio cappello, e quello è il mio libro. Quale cosa vuoi tu, e com'è la tua giornata?
npc.translation: I write in the book: "The jacket is nice. May I try it on?" Yes, you may try on the jacket, but only once. This is my hat, and that is my book. Which thing do you want, and how is your day?

player: Voglio questa giacca, non il cappello. Quanto costa? La mia giornata è lunga.

verdict.overallFeedback: Molto bene! You told Cuthbert you want this jacket and not the hat, asked the price, and shared that your day is long, all in good Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Passed: "Voglio questa giacca" correctly uses "questa" to say which one you want.

npc.narrative: The alba reaches the negozio without being asked, and the cielo is entirely sereno. Cuthbert Marrow turns the libro toward the finestra, as if the light might sign it. Outside, la strada looks a little più dritta than it did yesterday.
npc.native: Scrivo nel libro: «La mia giornata è lunga». Questa giacca costa dieci monete, e quello è il cappello: resta qui. Ora io non ho più una giacca, e questo è un problema per me. Che cosa fai oggi con la giacca, e com'è una giornata lunga per te?
npc.translation: I write in the book: "My day is long." This jacket costs ten coins, and that is the hat: it stays here. Now I no longer have a jacket, and this is a problem for me. What do you do today with the jacket, and what is a long day like for you?

player: Oggi cammino con la giacca, perché fa freddo. Ecco dieci monete. Mi dispiace per il problema!

npc.narrative: The alba comes up chiara over the negozio, and the strada outside is already fredda. You hand over the monete; Cuthbert counts them due volte, writes the numero in the libro, and regards the empty gancio where the giacca hung, like a tooth gone missing.
npc.native: Scrivo nel libro: «Mi dispiace per il problema». Dieci monete: è giusto, e ora la giacca è tua. Io ho ancora un cappello, una camicia e un paio di scarpe, ma solo uno di ogni cosa. Che cosa vuoi sapere del mio negozio, e dove cammini stamattina con la giacca?
npc.translation: I write in the book: "I am sorry about the problem." Ten coins: that is right, and now the jacket is yours. I still have a hat, a shirt and a pair of shoes, but only one of each thing. What do you want to know about my shop, and where are you walking this morning with the jacket?

player: Cammino al mercato. Perché hai solo uno di ogni cosa?

npc.narrative: The alba comes up chiaro over the strada, which looks a little più dritta than you remember. Cuthbert Marrow puts the cappello back on its gancio, exactly where the polvere says it has always been. He opens the libro to a pagina nuova and licks the matita.
npc.native: Scrivo nel libro: «Cammino al mercato». Ho solo uno di ogni cosa perché un cappello è un amico, e due cappelli sono una folla. Che cosa compri al mercato, e che cosa vuoi chiedere ancora del mio negozio?
npc.translation: I write in the book: "I walk to the market." I have only one of each thing because one hat is a friend, and two hats are a crowd. What do you buy at the market, and what else do you want to ask about my shop?

player: Ha ha! Al mercato compro pane e formaggio. Ti piace il formaggio?

npc.narrative: Cuthbert runs a dito down the libro until he reaches the last riga, then nods at it as though it had agreed. The alba comes in through the finestra and settles on the cappello, which has not moved all night. Beyond the porta, the strada is being very quiet about something.
npc.native: Scrivo nel libro: «Al mercato compro pane e formaggio». Sì, mi piace il formaggio, ma ho solo un formaggio a casa, e non lo mangio. Che cosa vuoi sapere di me, e com'è il mercato all'alba?
npc.translation: I write in the book: "At the market I buy bread and cheese." Yes, I like cheese, but I have only one cheese at home, and I do not eat it. What do you want to know about me, and what is the market like at dawn?
